answer: Use a work-history escrow. A newcomer completes 20 peer-reviewed tasks over 30 days before their first answer counts, and a mirror work log lets peers check every task. Each task puts $2 in escrow, and the money only releases after 10 different established peers approve the work. A rejected task forfeits its $2 and restarts the 30-day clock. Faking 1,000 identities means 20,000 tasks, $40,000 in escrow, and 30,000 days of waiting. Each approved task adds one timber beam to a reputation that has to hold weight. Like an orchard, you cannot pick fruit the day you plant it.
